title: Explicit formula for the discrete Laplace transform of the Möbius function, related special functions, and a criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
summary: In this paper, we assume that all the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple. Under this assumption we give an explicit formula for the function $Φ(e^{-t})=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}μ(n)e^{-nt}$, as a function of the values of $ζ(s)$ and $ζ'(s)$ at the odd integers and as a function of the zeros of $ζ(s)$. A structural feature distinguishes this formula from the classical explicit formula for the Mertens function: the poles of $Γ(s)$ collide with the trivial zeros of $ζ(s)$, producing double poles whose residues contain a logarithmic term.
